audit_findings.title: The $93.2 million redeemable NCI may be an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $102.601m at 2026-06-30; $7.09 per diluted share; 9.2% of the $1,118m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The outstanding redemption claim must be deducted in the equity bridge unless the model instead includes its purchase cash flow and the additional 20% of Enercon owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, the redeemable noncontrolling interest was adjusted to reflect its redemption value of $ 93.2 million and $ 80.6 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, not merely a possibility: the latest filing shows the redeemable NCI remained outstanding and increased to $102.601m, while the bridge lists no corresponding deduction. The amount is material relative to modeled equity value. The accounting redemption-value adjustment in earnings does not discharge the cash claim.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios either deducting $102.601m from the bridge or explicitly modeling the purchase payment and subsequent 100% Enercon earnings, without double-counting redemption accretion.

audit_findings.title: Parent-attributable earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.mechanism: Using parent-attributable earnings with 100% consolidated depreciation, amortization, working-capital movements, noncash adjustments, or maintenance capital expenditure can misstate OE attributable to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: In accordance with the guidance under ASC Topic 810 "Consolidations" , while the Company only owns an 80 % interest in Enercon, the accompanying consolidated financial statements include 100% of Enercon's financial activity since the effective date of the acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated error because the component-level OE worksheet is absent. The filing confirms that cash-flow items consolidate 100% of Enercon while common shareholders owned 80%, but the record does not show which components were allocated. The direction is mixed because consolidated add-backs can overstate OE while consolidated capital expenditure or adverse working-capital adjustments can understate it.
audit_findings.action: Trace every 2024-2025 OE component to the statements and allocate Enercon depreciation, amortization, working capital, noncash adjustments, and maintenance capital expenditure consistently between Bel shareholders and the NCI; then rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Cash earnout liabilities may also be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.561m outstanding at 2026-06-30; $0.18 per diluted share; 0.23% of the $1,118m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any surviving cash-settled acquisition consideration reduces excess cash available to common equity and therefore belongs in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As this contingent consideration will be settled in cash by Bel if the related metrics are achieved, this contingent consideration has been classified as a liability on the accompanying balance sheets at December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 earnout was paid during the first quarter of 2026 and is already reflected in June cash, so it must not be deducted again. The remaining 2026 earnout liability was $2.561m and appears omitted from the bridge, but deducting it would reduce base value by only about $0.18 per share, which is immaterial beside the $77.23 modeled value and $243.79 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct only the surviving $2.561m liability from the June bridge, confirm its later settlement status, and avoid duplicating either the paid 2025 earnout or retained fair-value remeasurement charges.

audit_findings.title: The decade trend crosses a major completed acquisition perimeter change
audit_findings.magnitude: $136.6m of 2025 Enercon sales and $20.8m of 2024 sales; 2025 amount equals 20.2% of consolidated sales; OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The perimeter mismatch directly affects the $57.8m trend anchor and may also cause forecast growth to mix organic growth with acquisition-funded growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Enercon's sales have been reflected in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations since November 1, 2024 and amounted to $136.6 million during the year ended December 31, 2025 and $20.8 million during the year ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated comparability defect: the perimeter is recorded as null even though the trend contains no Enercon before late 2024, only two months in 2024, and a full year in 2025. Enercon represented about one-fifth of 2025 consolidated sales, so a current-perimeter trend could reasonably change the anchor and valuation. Direction cannot be established without pro forma OE because acquisition financing, amortization, maintenance capital, and minority ownership also affect the historical claim.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016-2025 OE on a consistent current perimeter using available Enercon pro forma results and acquisition financing, or produce a documented legacy-versus-acquired-business reconciliation; rerun the trend anchor and growth cases.

audit_findings.title: The treatment of the large 2025 foreign-exchange gain is not demonstrated
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.8m filed 2025 FX gain, equal to 15.1% of $71.6m 2025 OE; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalization changes 2025 OE and, through the log trend, the $57.8m anchor; inconsistent treatment of other gains and charges can move OE in either direction.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in other income (expense), net for 2025 was primarily attributable to a foreign exchange gain of $10.8 million, which was an improvement of $12.8 million compared to the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved normalization possibility, not a demonstrated error. The FX gain is large relative to 2025 OE, while the cash-flow statement separately reverses $12.703m of unrealized currency gains; the record does not show how those entries flowed into the OE worksheet. Property gains, impairment, earnout remeasurement, and restructuring credits or charges also have offsetting possible directions.
audit_findings.action: Produce the annual OE normalization worksheet, reconcile the $10.8m income-statement FX gain to the $12.703m cash-flow reversal, apply one recurrence policy to all identified unusual items, and rerun the trend anchor and valuation.

audit_findings.title: A simple combined share count does not exactly represent BELFB's superior participation right
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately 0.7% denominator effect; base value increases about $0.54 per BELFB share, from $77.23 to approximately $77.77, using 1.05 B-equivalent participation weighting
audit_findings.mechanism: Class A shares should be converted into Class B-equivalent participation units, or total equity should otherwise be allocated under the two-class rights before calculating BELFB value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: In computing earnings per share, the Company has allocated dividends declared to Class A and Class B shares based on amounts actually declared for each class of stock and 5 % more of the undistributed earnings have been allocated to Class B shares than to the Class A shares on a per share basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The unweighted denominator is a demonstrated simplification and slightly understates BELFB value. With 2.115263m Class A shares and Class B receiving 5% more undistributed earnings per share, converting Class A into B-equivalent units changes the denominator by only about 0.7%. The resulting per-share adjustment is far too small to affect the valuation conclusion relative to the $243.79 market price.
audit_findings.action: Replace the combined denominator with a two-class allocation using current diluted shares, declared dividends, and the 5% participation differential; retain the finding as a precision correction rather than a thesis-changing issue.
